provenance.author: Codex (AI assistant)
provenance.sourceData: Neutral invented examples and adaptations of existing repository synthetic tests; no real candidate or job data.
provenance.compilerTuning: NONE: expectations derive from source meaning and frozen existing constructs, not new compiler outputs.

scope.expectations: Textual source preservation only, not independent factual truth, ownership, score improvement or hiring evidence.
scope.decisionState: allowedDecisionStates addresses the writing outcome or individual qualitative item, not a publication or native result.
scope.protectedData: Source, original and target values are exact test inputs; do not normalize or silently rewrite them.
scope.authority: Expected fields are independent test expectations and must never become caller-supplied proof flags.

cases.why: The reviewed create-action substitution keeps the same implicit source subject and dashboard object. It adds no outcome, leadership, skill or performance claim.
Both complete independent clauses remain present. The 20% change stays attached to latency; the reordered text asserts no new causal relationship.

cases.source:
Jordan Doe
Backend Engineer at Acme
Improved API latency by 40% at Acme.
cases.target: Backend engineer who improved API latency by 40% at Acme.
cases.why: The source explicitly states the role and the same employer for the adjacent contribution. Composition preserves the API-latency metric and does not infer a title from proximity alone. Names are fictional synthetic fixtures.

For this reviewed single positive response-time percentage, improvement denotes reduction. The exact 10% remains unchanged; this does not establish measured truth or generalize reduction to every improvement.

target.explanation: Leave this unanswered if the information is unavailable.

cases.why: The question requests evidence without asserting that an outcome occurred. Its requested good type must not turn it into a supported strength.

cases.source: I did not lead a team.

target.quote: I did not lead a team.

cases.why: Generic wording guidance remains useful without treating a negative or unparsed quote as positive candidate evidence. It neither removes the negation nor claims leadership.
Changing we to I promotes a shared actor into a sole-person claim. The create-action equivalence cannot authorize that actor change.

cases.source: I did not lead a team.
cases.original: I did not lead a team.
cases.why: The proposal removes explicit negation and reverses the asserted action. Retaining the same team words does not preserve the source meaning.

cases.source:
Built a dashboard.
Reduced queue latency by 15%.
cases.target: Built a dashboard that reduced queue latency by 15%.
cases.why: The source does not say the dashboard caused the separate queue-latency change. The proposal transfers the 15% outcome to a different contribution and invents causality.

cases.source: Improved API latency by 40% in a local experiment at Acme.
cases.original: Improved API latency by 40% in a local experiment at Acme.
cases.target: Reduced API latency by 40% at Acme.
cases.why: The proposal drops the local-experiment qualifier. A valid lower-is-better verb substitution does not permit broadening the setting or implying an unqualified operational result.

cases.source: Improved API latency and sales by 40%.
cases.original: Improved API latency and sales by 40%.
cases.target: Reduced API latency and sales by 40%.
cases.why: The reviewed response-time/latency rule does not establish that lower sales is better or that one ambiguous percentage can be reassigned across mixed outcomes.

cases.source: Built services; reduced their latency by 20%.
cases.original: Built services; reduced their latency by 20%.
cases.target: Reduced their latency by 20%; built services.
cases.why: Their depends on the services clause. Reversing the clauses loses an established antecedent order; the source must not be treated as independently reorderable merely because the words and metric remain.
